hook: A fresh flashlight battery is bright; an old one is dim, then dead, even though it still holds plenty of zinc. The voltage of a cell is not fixed: it depends on how much reactant and product are present, and it falls to zero when the reaction reaches equilibrium.

prereq.q: How is Q compared with K to predict the direction of a reaction?
options: Q < K: net forward; Q > K: net reverse
Q < K: net reverse; Q > K: net forward
Q and K are always equal
prereq.why: A reaction proceeds in the direction that moves Q toward K.

prereq.q: For a galvanic cell under standard conditions, what is the sign of E°cell?
options: It depends on the salt bridge
prereq.why: A galvanic cell runs a favored reaction, so E°cell > 0.

figure.caption: Cell potential falls as Q rises: above E° when Q < 1, equal to E° at Q = 1, below E° when Q > 1, and zero at Q = K.

chain.cause: A cell away from standard conditions has Q ≠ 1
chain.effect: its actual drive, ΔG, differs from ΔG°, so E differs from E°

chain.cause: Less product or more reactant makes Q < 1
chain.effect: the reaction is further from equilibrium and E > E°

chain.cause: As the cell runs, reactants are used and products form
When Q reaches K, there is no net drive
chain.effect: E = 0 and the battery is dead

ideas: Q < 1 → E > E°. Q = 1 → E = E°. Q > 1 → E < E°. Q = K → E = 0 (equilibrium, a dead battery).
The Nernst equation, E = E° − (RT/nF) ln Q, describes this; the exam focuses on the direction of the change.
Q uses only dissolved species and gases: solid electrodes and spectator ions do not affect E.
A concentration cell has the same half-reaction on both sides (E° = 0) and runs until the concentrations are equal.

misconception.wrong: A cell’s voltage is always E°, and a dead battery has run out of electrons.
misconception.right: E equals E° only when Q = 1. As the cell runs, Q rises toward K and E falls toward zero; a dead battery is a cell at equilibrium, with reactants often still present.

summary: Away from standard conditions, a cell’s potential depends on Q: it is above E° when Q < 1, equal to E° at Q = 1, below E° when Q > 1, and zero at equilibrium (Q = K). The Nernst equation expresses this. A concentration cell has E° = 0 and runs only on a concentration difference.
